set.approach: Use the upper lot at Jackson Hole ski area, behind Teton Mountain Lodge, and walk the paved McCollister Road toward the Union Pass lift until it dead-ends. A small trail leaves to the left; take it to a service road, turn left, and follow the road as it steepens into a trail up to the buttress. Another way in is to ride the tram, take the Rock Springs Loop trail along the ridge toward Cody Peak, bear left onto a road, then right at the next junction onto what is the Rendezvous ski trail in winter; look on the right for a cairned climbers' trail that drops into the base of the buttress. The West Sector is reached after crossing the creek to the talus field and is the furthest left (west), flanked on its right by a steep gully; from the tram it is the first crag met on the way down into Rock Springs Canyon.

review.notes: Rock Springs Buttress page: approaches; West Sector page: location. The route page gives no usable start position.

set.approach: Park at Enormodome Camp on Forest Service Road 391 (Schoolhouse Park Road), the left fork at the Hunter Creek Trailhead turnoff on Highway 16 west of Buffalo. Follow a faint path north out of camp along the edge of the woods to a cattle trail heading northeast toward the big meadow. After a short distance leave the cattle trail and skirt the boggy meadow on its north side until a cleared path through the young forest runs straight to the south prow of the dome. Charitable Contribution is the fourth route from the left on the east face.
set.descent_text: Lower off the clip-and-lower anchors at the top; the anchors have lowering carabiners.

review.notes: Overview page: approach from camp and stainless hardware with biners for lowering; route page: position on the face and clip-and-lower anchors.

set.approach: Freak Mountain is remote and reached along Forest Service Road 352, a long motorized route; carry the USGS topographic map and the Forest Service road map. The panels are wavy dolomite walls with only a few routes. Keep on Trucking is on a square block just right of The Missing Years, the most prominent and longest line on the wall.

review.notes: Area page: the Forest Service road and map advice; route page: position beside The Missing Years.

set.approach: Park in the climbers' lot on the north side of the highway at the west end of Shoshone Canyon, between the second short tunnel and the long tunnel. The Island is the plug of granite directly in front of the lot, only seconds away. Boomstick starts a short way right of In With The New, in the corner, and follows the face just left of the corner.
set.descent_text: Lower from the sport anchor. This is the longest single pitch on The Island, so use a rope long enough to reach the ground and knot its end.

review.notes: Route page: position and rope warning; area pages: parking and the Island.

review.notes: Route page: neighbours; area pages: parking and the Island. No descent stated.

set.approach: Clark is north of Cody on Wyoming Highway 120, near the Montana line. Turn west at the Edelweiss Restaurant onto Canyon Road 1AB and follow it to the mouth of Clark's Fork Canyon, where the north massif is hard to miss. From the highway, cross a BLM fence and walk a short way to the routes. Milky Way is the second route from the left.

review.notes: Area page: road and walk-in; route page: second from the left (the page does not name the wall). Filed under Cody here, but Mountain Project files The Mouth under Clarks Fork Canyon.

set.approach: Ride the gondola or the tram and take the Cirque Trail to the boulder; walking up from the valley floor also works but is far more work. Free Beer Tastes Better climbs the southeast arete of the boulder.

review.notes: Area page: access by gondola or tram on the Cirque Trail; route page: southeast arete. No descent stated.

set.approach: Reach the parking area by Monument Hill Road off Highway 120 north of Cody, and not by Rattlesnake Creek Road. From the parking area, drop down the big scree gully along the south side of the Africa Son palisade to the base of the route.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route. Scramble to the top anchor on a large ledge a short way below the summit; the upper rappel stations are rigged with cord and rings, so carry spare cord or quicklinks.

review.notes: Route page: scree gully access, top anchor on a ledge below the summit, rappel the route. Single source for each.

set.approach: Starting at the Blacktail lot, head south on the well-developed trail as it climbs and crosses a small creek; after that, look for a trail on the left through the talus. It leads to the Middle Wall and continues to the Upper Wall. stHank-O is just left of Blitzkrieg and right of a choss gully, following an obvious black and blue streak.

review.notes: Area page: the trail to the Upper Wall; route page: position by Blitzkrieg. No descent stated.

set.approach: Park at Enormodome Camp on Forest Service Road 391 (Schoolhouse Park Road), the left fork at the Hunter Creek Trailhead turnoff on Highway 16 west of Buffalo. Follow a faint path north out of camp along the edge of the woods to a cattle trail heading northeast toward the big meadow. After a short distance leave the cattle trail and skirt the boggy meadow on its north side until a cleared path through the young forest runs straight to the south prow of the dome. Mid-face on the west side, a natural staircase allows a third-class scramble to the top. Beer-Fueled Blowhards Do Good is the third route in from the south end of the west face, sharing its start with Beer Potomaniacs.
set.descent_text: Lower off the clip-and-lower anchors at the top; the anchors have lowering carabiners.
